script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Drama
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

The air is thick with the sweet aroma of freshly brewed coffee and the buzz of chatter and clinking dishes. At the counter, JEN (mid-30s, kind eyes, dressed casually) orders a latte.

JEN
(looking at a picture on her phone)
(sighs)

 waits for her drink. Next to her, LUCAS (early 40s, rugged, wearing a suit) sets down a stack of papers and orders an espresso.

LUCAS
(looking up, sees Jen)
Jen, right? I'm Lucas. We met at the fundraiser last week.

JEN
(smiling)
Oh, yes. Nice to see you again.

They share a moment of awkward silence. Jen takes a sip of her latte.

LUCAS
So, I was thinking about what we talked about last week. I know it's a long shot, but I wanted to ask if you'd be willing to give me a chance to make it right.

Jen hesitates, then hands him her business card.

JEN
Alright, Lucas. I'll meet with you, but no promises.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jen paces her small apartment, staring at her reflection in the mirror. Her past mistakes haunt her.

JEN
(to herself)
What am I doing? I can't trust him.

She takes a deep breath and sits down at her kitchen table, staring at the business card.

INT. LUCAS' OFFICE - DAY

Lucas sits at his desk, shuffling papers and looking worried. Jen knocks on the door.

LUCAS
(smiling)
Come in, Jen.

They exchange polite greetings and Lucas offers her a seat.

LUCAS
(leaning forward)
Look, Jen, I know I made mistakes in the past. I've learned from them, and I want to make things right. I'll do whatever it takes.

JEN
(skeptical)
What does that mean, exactly?

Lucas hesitates, then lays out a detailed plan to make amends for his past mistakes. Jen listens intently, her expression softening.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

They sit across from each other, sipping their drinks.

JEN
(smiling)
I'll give you a chance, Lucas. But this is all on your terms.

Lucas nods, relieved. They spend the afternoon talking, laughing, and reconnecting.

INT. JEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Jen stands in her living room, looking at a picture of her and Lucas. She takes a deep breath and dials a number.

JEN
(on the phone)
Hi, Dad. I have some news.

INT. LUCAS' APARTMENT - NIGHT

Lucas sits at his desk, staring at a blank piece of paper. He looks up as his phone rings.

Lucas
(answering)
Hi, Jen.

JEN
(on the phone)
I've decided to give you a chance, Lucas. But there's something I need to tell you first.

They share a moment of silence, then Jen tells him about her father. Lucas listens intently, offering words of support and encouragement.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Jen and Lucas sit across from each other, holding hands.

JEN
(smiling)
I'm glad we had this chance to reconnect, Lucas. I really am.

LUCAS
(squeezing her hand)
Me too, Jen. Me too.

They sit in comfortable silence, watching the world go by.

FADE OUT.

THE END
